purpose: overhead of pacha recording on a train verb vs the EXT-04 noise band (FALSIFY-EXT-004 overhead clause)
host: lambda-vector (CPU only; no GPU used, R-9 respected)
build: debug (dev profile) test binary at worktree HEAD 349dc91e0 + blake3-only input hashing; release is faster, so these are upper bounds
harness: cargo test -p apr-cli --lib ext05_recorder_overhead_receipt -- --ignored --nocapture (EXT05_BASE_MB sets base size); tmp pacha home on /mnt/nvme-raid0
workload: base file N MB, dataset dir 50 MB + 2 small files, produced adapter 50 MB
host_load: load average 19-43 from other fleet work (shared host, not clean-room)
structure: the recorder runs once before and once after the verb, outside the training step loop, so steady tok/s (the EXT-04 metric) is unchanged by construction; the cost is fixed wall time
verdict: PASS: added wall time is <=2.4 s per run (<0.5 s at start). That is under 18.63% of any run longer than ~13 s; every real finetune/pretrain run is minutes or more
finding: the first cut hashed inputs with blake3+sha256 in one pass: 25.0 s start for a 1 GB base in debug. Inputs need only blake3 (pacha's content address), and that brought start to 0.41 s. sha256 is computed only for the produced artifact
